title: Hello, my name is Kristopher Huang
text:
About Me
I am a highly curious, hard-working, eager-to-learn, and willing-to-help person. I like to learn about topics that interest me and do my share of work, possibly more, so that others have to do less. My favorite activities include reading, exercising, researching whatever topic that interests me, gaming, gardening, and watching wrestling.
I am interested in the field of marketing, specifically General Marketing, because it’s a versatile field and the ways that the marketing field works interests me. In the future, I am looking to get into a field of marketing that involves brand research, marketing toward demographics, or marketing involving seasonal, collaborative, and limited-time events, as these aspects are ones I’m most interested in.
Currently, as of writing this on April 26, 2026, I am a senior at Cal Poly Pomona enrolled in the College of Business Administration as a student in International Business and Marketing. I am expecting to complete my degree in General Marketing in the Fall of 2026 and graduate in the Spring of 2027.



My Goals
My current goals in life include:

Finding a good-paying and fulfilling job in the Marketing field.
Learn as much as I can about topics that I’m interested in.
Become better at cooking.
Explore my surroundings and learn about local businesses, wildlife, and plants.
Try many different kinds of foods from different countries and cultures.
Be a useful and helpful person whenever I can.




Connect With Me
If you would like to connect with me, you can contact me at my Gmail, kristopherlxhuang@gmail.com, or connect with my LinkedIn.

title: My Projects
text:
Teamwork is essential when working in Marketing. Over the years, I’ve done a number of group projects for several Marketing classes at Cal Poly Pomona or projects that relate to Marketing. Here are some of the projects I’ve worked on alongside my classmates.


Accounting in the Coca-Cola Company - ACC 2070

This project was done for ACC 2070 - Financial Accounting For Decision Making.
It focuses on the Accounting aspects of the Coca-Cola Company, such as Accounting Practices, Income Statements, and Balance Sheets. The presentation highlights things like Financial Highlights, Accounting Ethics, and Controversies surrounding its practices.
The full PDF of the presentation can be viewed here.



Kroger Company Analysis - MHR 3010

This project was done for MHR 3010 - Principles of Management.
Our group did an analysis on the important aspects of Kroger’s management, including Organizing, Leading, and Controlling, as well as a SWOT analysis. The presentation details how Kroger’s management aspects affect things such as decision making, communications, strategies, employee benefits, and workplace conditions.
The full PDF of the presentation can be viewed here.



Bay Law Promotional Strategies - IBM 3072

This project was done for IBM 3072 - Promotional Strategies.
As the name of the class implies, the purpose of this project was for us to come up with a promotional strategy for the Bay Law Injury Attorney firm. To do so, we analyzed a variety of factors including their competitors, location and demographic data, media presence, and performing a SWOT analysis. Through them, we came up with a strategy that accounted for target demographics, budget, costs, Return on Investment, and online activity.
The full PDF of the presentation can be viewed here.



Starbucks Loyalty Program - IBM 4022

This project was done for IBM 4022 - Brand Impression and Management.
Our group was assigned a case on Starbucks’ loyalty program and how it shaped the business, its practices shaping its customer-based brand equity, the technology-focused aspects shaping its identity, and its social media presence and mobile app being iconic among its consumer base.
The full PDF of the presentation can be viewed here.

title: General Marketing
text:
I’ve chosen my future role in a marketing career to be in General Marketing. Below details how and why I came to the decision.


My Initial Choice
Before I became interested in Marketing, my initial choice was Computer Engineering. I figured that I could use the skills I gained to work with my own computers at home, such as fixing problems or improving their performance. However, I feel that a career in this field isn’t viable for me for a couple of reasons:

Programming can be complicated and frustrating for me sometimes. The last thing I want to happen is to get stuck trying to solve a coding problem while on a tight schedule and getting frustrated at being unable to figure out what to do.
A lot of programming is involved. I’m okay with doing a bit of it once in a while, but working a job that involves doing it constantly is overwhelming.
There are just so many functions and arguments to memorize. Without a complete guide or AI, I would have no idea what to do with certain assignments.

I also thought about getting into video game development since I like playing video games in my spare time, but standard coding is already complicated enough and doing it for video games is whole new can of worms, so I decided against it.



The Business Administration Major Classes
While taking the required classes for my Business Administration Major, I formed an opinion on the options based on my experiences in the classes. The classes I liked the least are Accounting, Technology and Operations Management, and Finance, Real Estate, and Law. The reason is due to one thing the classes have in common: Highly Complicated Word Problems.
While I’m fine with doing math equations, word problems are what really make my head hurt and cause my frustration to surface. They can contain irrelevant information, word things in a way that confuses you, and ask you to create and solve equations from what mish-mash of information you are given instead of having something simple and straightforward. The reason I’m able to pass these classes is because I have the foresight to take detailed notes for my assignments and exams.
On the other hand, I find that Management and Human Resources, Economics, and International Business and Marketing are more lax in comparison. MHR and IBM have group presentations, which I’m fine with doing as long as everyone pulls their weight, and EC’s math problems are simpler and not overly complicated.



Interest in Marketing
My interest in the Marketing option started growing when I took IBM 3012 - Principles of Marketing Management. Several topics caught my interest, such as brand imagery, sensory marketing, marketing mediums, social media marketing, and importing and exporting. My interest increased further when I started taking more courses for the IBM option in the Fall 2025 Semester. It got to the point where I started using AI to research more about marketing topics and scenarios. As for the type of Marketing I chose, I went with General Marketing because it’s the most well-rounded of the choices. I’m a person who prefers balanced choices over specialized ones because I like to be able to do a bit of everything and help out in different fields. For example, at a job, I can work in advertising, but if the social media marketing team needs some help, I can lend a hand.

title: My Skills
text:
I’ve always been told that I’m a smart person with a high IQ that’s capable of doing anything if I put my mind to it, and I’d like to believe that in order to maintain a positive self-image of myself. This page details the skills I possess that can be useful in a casual or job setting.


Creativity
I’ve always had an active and wide imagination, always thinking of scenarios in my head, such as a fictional adventure for a character, creating scenes and interactions in sandbox video games like Garry’s Mod, and thinking of my own concepts for things that interest me, such as futuristic mechanical tools that can be used to make jobs easier. I often get inspiration from works of others, such as written stories and artworks.
I can come up with solutions to different problems depending on the scenario and the tools I’m given to work with. An example is using an old skateboard as a trolley to move heavy objects around at home. In a working environment, I would have to ask others, especially a higher-up, for their thoughts in order to avoid jumping the gun and getting in trouble. I think I would thrive in a job that requires me to use my creativity to come up with concepts and designs, such as a concept artist.



Fast Learner
I often find myself learning about something fairly quick, sometimes through correct assumptions based on what I’m shown. For example, in a new video game, I can figure out the controls, mechanics, and gimmicks within a couple of minutes from just testing things out.
If I’m given specific instructions on how to do something, I will be able to follow along. Once I do that task enough, I’ll be able to remember it. An example is math, one of the subjects I’ve often been told I’m good at. I’ve grown so accustomed to certain mathematical concepts, that if you show me an equation, I’ll be able to figure out the order of operations and which variables produce what values.
In a work setting, I’ll be willing to learn as much as I can about my job through listening to what I’m told, doing the task until I get the hang of it, and asking questions for specific situations. Once I get the gist of everything, I can handle things without too much issue.



Organization
I’m a firm believer that organization being one of the most important traits a person should possess. Without it, we would be scrambling helplessly, unable to find what we’re looking for through an unkempt mess.
When it comes to the work I do, I always categorize them and keep things consistent. For example, for my classes, I always create a folder for each one to store things related to them. Then I create subfolders for different types of things in that class, such as homework assignments and project elements.
My need for organization even extends to minor things. For example, if I come across a book on a shelf that fell over or is in the wrong place, I’ll take a few seconds to straighten it out.



Dedication
Getting things done before a deadline is critical. Not only does it ensure you have time to look things over for mistakes, but it shows that you are serious about giving your best effort, and it nets you some spare time to rest and enjoy yourself after doing some hard work. “All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy” after all. Completing all of my tasks early removes a massive weight from my chest.
In school, I always made it a priority to get my schoolwork done so I don’t have to worry about it later. It gives me time to both relax and study if there’s a test coming up.
I’ve been taught to “take the initiative” whenever I can. It essentially means that I should do what needs to be done without being told. An example is that if I notice a mess in a workspace, I should clean it up instead of waiting for someone to tell me to. It shows that I’m committed to working hard and understand what I’m supposed to do.



Team Player
Teamwork is important when it comes to tasks that require multiple participants to get done. While I may not be leader material, I’m always willing to give my all on whatever part I’m given. I’m willing to communicate, coordinate, listen to feedback, and take one for the team when a situation calls for it.
On the other hand, I do have worries when it comes to being a team player, namely teammates not doing their parts and slacking behind and coming off as nagging or pushy if I communicate too fervently. I want to make sure that everyone is on the same page and that the working environment for everyone is positive, hassle-free, and flexible.
